enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1047 PM MST Wed Nov 4 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... Updated at 130 PM MST Wed Nov 4 2026

 - Quiet weather with near to slightly below normal temperatures.

 - Increasing chances for light rain showers Friday night into
   Saturday, with an upper level disturbance moving through.
   

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 956 PM MST Wed Nov 4 2026

Temperatures will drop through the rest of the night as the
shortwave trough moves past New Mexico. Some lowland desert spots
in the Tularosa and Jornada could fall into the upper 30s, though
no new freeze areas are expected. High temperatures for Thursday 
will run about 2 to 5 degrees below average (upper 60s-low 70s), 
with the exception of the Lower Valley, which will run about 1 to 
2 degrees above seasonal averages (mid to upper 70s). Winds will 
be generally from the north at 5 to 10 mph, and conditions will be
relatively dry.

Temperatures will fall again on Friday, close to 4 to 6 degrees
below average. A deep trough and weak southeasterly push or backdoor cold front
will bring increasing chances for light rain showers Friday night
into Saturday. The GFS has caught up with the ECMWF with cutting
off the trough into a cutoff low and slowing it down over the
region Friday night and into Saturday, increasing the QPF to
around 0.1 for the lowlands. The next couple of runs should see
the QPF increase, so we will need to keep watch for how heavy this
rain event will be. PWATS at this time for Friday and Saturday are
hovering around 0.6", so flooding is unlikely to be a risk, though
it can't be ruled out if the QPF gets heavier. Dry weather returns
on Sunday as an upper-level high moves into the region.

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 956 PM MST Wed Nov 4 2026

VFR conditions will persist throughout the period as skies remain
clear. Winds through the day will blow predominantly from the
north at 5 to 10 kt. KDMN could see some gusts up to 20 kt around
18Z.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 105 PM MST Wed Nov 4 2026

Low fire weather concerns as lingering effects of rainfall keep
ERC values high. Slightly below normal temperatures the next few
days will also promote strong radiational cooling at night, and
excellent RH recovery even in the lowland deserts, while afternoon
minimum RH values stay above 25 percent in the low elevations, 
and 40 percent at high elevations.

An upper level disturbance will bring some light rain chances to
the area this weekend, favoring the higher terrain as usual, but
also lowlands east of the Rio Grande.

&&
